o1.biggest_strength: Threshold maths is sharp and honest: the ₹599 case with an explicit walk-away break-even, and it explicitly protects the serum reorder that Ishita lives on.
o1.biggest_mistake: The serum+lip balm bundle leans on the lip balm over the actual top pair (face wash + serum), so its bundle ladder is built around a lower-value add-on rather than the proven ₹944 routine.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Make face wash + serum the headline routine bundle at a modest saving with the margin shown, keep lip balm as the cart add-on, and bring COD/RTO cost into the threshold decision instead of treating every order alike.

o2.biggest_strength: Bundles map to how customers already buy (face wash+serum, shampoo+conditioner, body lotion+body wash) with break-even maths that shows the cost of discounting existing pair buyers, plus the lip balm as threshold add-on and a COD-fee test.
o2.biggest_mistake: Choosing to keep ₹499 as the recommendation is defensible but undersells the brief's ask to actually work the money on moving it, and the lakh-level projections carry wide ranges that read as soft.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Recommend a clear threshold move (or a prepaid-only lower bar) with COD/RTO fully costed, tighten the projection ranges to one number per scenario, and say it in the owner's voice rather than in test-table shorthand.

reason: Output 2 picks the bundles customers already buy and treats COD refusals as the real leak, so I'd act on it; Output 1's threshold maths is crisper but its bundle ladder is built on the wrong pair and it leaves COD out of the shipping decision.
